items.title: How the Bayeux Tapestry Got to the British Museum
items.author: Alex Marshall
items.content: <article>French art experts insisted the fragile 900-year-old masterpiece could never travel. Political will, cutting-edge engineering and unorthodox diplomacy proved them wrong.</article>

items.title: The Evening: Primary Voters Go to the Polls
items.author: Evan Gorelick
items.content: <article>Plus, Iran exploits dwindling U.S. interceptors. Here’s the latest at the end of Tuesday.</article>

items.title: With El-Sayed’s Victory Comes a Wave of Islamophobia
items.author: Jennifer Medina
items.content: <article>As Muslim politicians like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan have become more prominent, they have experienced considerable bigotry. President Trump said Democrats were electing “jihadists.”</article>

items.title: How Iran Adapted Its Attacks as U.S. War Munitions Dwindled
items.author: Eric Schmitt and Helene Cooper
items.content: <article>The Iranian strikes that killed three U.S. soldiers in Jordan show how quickly Iran’s war-fighting skills have evolved, as the Pentagon runs low on interceptors.</article>

items.title: Mamdani to Abandon Plan to Replace Elizabeth Street Garden With Housing
items.author: Mihir Zaveri and Dana Rubinstein
items.content: <article>After more than a decade, the fight over an effort to build affordable housing on the site of a community garden in Manhattan is winding down.</article>

items.title: Ocasio-Cortez Opened Up About Freezing Her Eggs. She Got Women Talking.
items.author: Juliet Macur and Anemona Hartocollis
items.content: <article>Many women say being open about the fertility treatment is a form of empowerment. But critics say all the talk can be misleading.</article>

items.title: El-Sayed’s Winning Path in Michigan
items.author: Thomas L. Friedman
items.content: <article>A swing-state Democratic Senate nominee needs to keep saying this: Jews have a right to a Jewish homeland.</article>

items.title: As Death Toll From Colombia Earthquake Rises to at Least 181, Rescuers Hunt for Survivors
items.author: Genevieve Glatsky and Julie Turkewitz
items.content: <article>“We heard them screaming,” said one rescuer in Cali, where emergency workers and volunteers are racing against time to find the living trapped in the rubble.</article>

items.title: University of Michigan Will Ease Up on Grades for Student Mental Health
items.author: Mark Arsenault
items.content: <article>The university will make first-semester grades pass or fail, to encourage students to try different classes and lessen fears of what a low grade could mean.</article>

items.title: What We Know About the Earthquake in Colombia
items.author: John Yoon
items.content: <article>The 7.4-magnitude quake, which killed more than 100 people and damaged hundreds of buildings, was the strongest recorded in Colombia in a decade.</article>

items.title: Trump Said to Have Secretly Used Military Jet to Leave Turkey Amid Threats From Iran
items.author: Maggie Haberman, Eric Schmitt and Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>President Trump hid in an airport catering container and was taken to a military jet for a secret flight out of country after the NATO summit last month.</article>

items.title: What to Know About the Vaccines Targeted by Trump’s Executive Order
items.author: Maggie Astor, Dani Blum and Teddy Rosenbluth
items.content: <article>The order, whose legal power is unclear, recommended narrowing the use of vaccinations against several diseases that can be life-threatening.</article>

items.title: Before Trump’s Catering Container Ruse, Other Presidents Obscured Risky Travel Plans
items.author: Claire Moses
items.content: <article>President Trump was part of a particularly elaborate deception last month, boarding one jet before being spirited away to another.</article>

items.title: A 5th Summer Heat Wave Will Hit Europe This Week. Here’s What to Know.
items.author: Nazaneen Ghaffar
items.content: <article>The latest heat wave is the fifth to batter European countries since May as scientists warn that the continent is warming faster than any other.</article>

items.title: Can Nebraska’s Definitely-Not-a-Democrat Candidate Crack the G.O.P. Hold on Red America?
items.author: Michelle Cottle
items.content: <article>The Democratic brand is just too toxic in large swaths of the country.</article>

items.title: The U.S. Missile Stockpile Is Dangerously Low
items.author: Natalie Kitroeff, Eric Schmidt, Michael Simon Johnson, Chris Benderev, Chris Haxel, Paige Cowett, Dan Powell, Diane Wong and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>The United States’ war with Iran has caused a critical weaponry shortage. That leaves the U.S. military vulnerable and complicates Washington’s efforts to end the war.</article>
